props.title: The Object of My Affection

sections.content: The Object of My Affection (1998) sits at a fascinating intersection of 90s romantic comedies and LGBTQ+ representation, arriving just months before Will & Grace would debut on television. Jennifer Aniston and Paul Rudd's chemistry drives this unconventional love story about a straight woman falling for her gay best friend. The film broke ground by treating George's sexuality matter-of-factly rather than as a punchline, while exploring the complex emotions of platonic love versus romantic attraction. It shares DNA with other boundary-pushing 90s romances like Chasing Amy (1997) and My Best Friend's Wedding (1997), which challenged traditional romantic comedy formulas.

sections.content: Director Nicholas Hytner, fresh off The Crucible (1996), brings his theatrical sensibilities to the intimate New York settings. The film's exploration of chosen family and non-traditional relationships predicted themes that would become more prevalent in 2000s cinema like The Kids Are All Right (2010) and Beginners (2010). Paul Rudd's sensitive portrayal of George avoided stereotypes common in 90s depictions of gay characters, while Jennifer Aniston proved her dramatic range beyond her Friends persona.

The film's handling of pregnancy and co-parenting arrangements was ahead of its time, predating similar explorations in films like The Switch (2010) and Friends with Kids (2011). While some critics at the time dismissed it as a conventional romantic comedy, its nuanced treatment of sexuality, friendship, and modern family structures feels remarkably current. The film's bittersweet ending - refusing easy resolution - distinguishes it from typical rom-com fare of the era. SUBHEAD: Evolution of LGBTQ+ Romance in Mainstream Cinema

sections.content: The Object of My Affection helped pave the way for more nuanced LGBTQ+ stories in mainstream cinema. While earlier films like Philadelphia (1993) focused on social issues, and In & Out (1997) played sexuality for broad comedy, this film treated its gay character's romantic life with the same weight as its straight characters. This approach influenced later works like The Next Best Thing (2000) and eventually led to more diverse storytelling in films like Happiest Season (2020).
